issues.legal_issue: A special-purpose land acquisition scheme is not invalid under equality review merely because it differs from the general acquisition law, where its procedures and compensation provisions are not arbitrary or unreasonable.
material_facts: The scheme authorised acquisition for defined welfare purposes after the landowner and other interested persons were invited to show cause.
The acquiring authority was required to consider the objections before deciding whether acquisition was necessary.
Compensation was based on market value as of the acquisition notice, determined after an inquiry in which interested persons could present their claims and evidence.
A person dissatisfied with the compensation determination could appeal to a court, and a further appeal was available in qualifying cases.
The scheme provided for interest if compensation was not paid or deposited by the time possession was taken.
issues.conclusion: The scheme's provisions were not violative of Article 14, except for the provision requiring compensation to be paid in instalments.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 14, a statute is invalid if it is so arbitrary or unreasonable that it must be struck down. A law of one State cannot be invalidated merely by comparing it with a law on the same subject derived from another source: State of M.P. v. G.C. Mandawar and Sant Lal Bharti v. State of Punjab. A comparable statute may be considered only as an indication of what may be reasonable. The Court found the acquisition procedure substantially encapsulated the safeguards in Sections 4 to 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; the market-value standard was an adequate compensation principle under State of Gujarat v. Shantilal Mangaldas. The Court also relied on Raja Harish Chandra Raj Singh v. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer and Periyar and Pareekanni Rubbers Ltd. v. State of Kerala in considering the compensation inquiry and appeal arrangements.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_special_purp: A person challenges the constitutionality of a statutory scheme for acquiring land for a defined public welfare purpose.
predicates.owners_receive_opportunity_to_object: The acquiring authority calls on landowners and other interested persons to explain why their land should not be acquired.
predicates.objections_are_considered_before_acquisi: The acquiring authority considers the objections before deciding whether to acquire the land.
predicates.compensation_is_based_on_market_value_af: The authority determines compensation by reference to market value after an inquiry that allows interested persons to present their claims and evidence.
predicates.dissatisfied_owners_can_seek_judicial_re: A person dissatisfied with the compensation determination can ask a court to review it.

issues.definition: When a special-purpose acquisition scheme is challenged and the owners can object, have those objections considered, receive market-value compensation determined after inquiry, and seek judicial review of compensation, the scheme is valid under equality review apart from any requirement to pay compensation in instalments.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory requirement to pay land-acquisition compensation in instalments is unreasonable and violates equality guarantees when the owner needs compensation in place of the land taken.
material_facts: The scheme required compensation above a small threshold to be paid in equal annual instalments rather than as a lump sum.
The Court considered that an owner would need compensation promptly to establish a new residence, acquire other agricultural land, or otherwise re-establish themselves.
The instalment requirement could be severed without invalidating the rest of the scheme.
issues.conclusion: The provision requiring payment of compensation in instalments was unconstitutional under Article 14 and was severed; compensation had to be paid in a lump sum.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 prohibits statutory provisions that are arbitrary or unreasonable. The Court held that delaying compensation through instalments was wholly unreasonable because an owner needs compensation in place of the land to re-establish themselves. The provision was severable, so only the instalment requirement was struck down.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_compensation: A constitutional challenge concerns the method by which compensation for acquired land is paid.
predicates.compensation_is_paid_in_installments: The law requires compensation to be paid in multiple payments over time rather than in a lump sum.
predicates.owner_needs_prompt_substitute_compensati: The owner needs the compensation promptly to obtain a substitute residence, land, or other means of re-establishing themselves.

issues.definition: If a challenged law pays compensation in instalments while the owner needs prompt substitute compensation, the instalment requirement is unconstitutional.

issues.legal_issue: A land-acquisition scheme for slum clearance is not invalid merely because it does not provide solatium for compulsory acquisition.
material_facts: The slum-clearance acquisition provisions were substantially similar to the other special-purpose acquisition scheme, except that they provided no solatium.
The slum-clearance provisions did not require compensation to be paid in instalments.
The Court considered that the acquired land was slum land and that the public interest in maintaining public services also mattered.
issues.conclusion: The slum-clearance acquisition provisions were intra vires the Constitution notwithstanding the absence of solatium.
issues.legal_principle: In Prakash Amichand Shah v. State of Gujarat, a Constitution Bench held that there is no general rule requiring the State always to pay solatium in addition to reasonable compensation, because the public interest is also important. The Court applied that principle to acquisition of slum land and found the absence of solatium not unreasonable.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_slum_clearan: A person challenges the constitutionality of a statutory scheme for acquiring land for slum clearance.
predicates.scheme_provides_reasonable_compensation: The scheme provides compensation for the acquired land that is otherwise reasonable.
predicates.scheme_does_not_require_installment_paym: The scheme does not require compensation to be paid in instalments.
predicates.scheme_provides_no_solatium: The scheme does not provide an additional payment because the acquisition is compulsory.

issues.definition: If a challenged slum-clearance scheme provides reasonable compensation without requiring instalments, the absence of an additional compulsory-acquisition payment does not make the scheme unconstitutional.

issues.legal_issue: A special acquisition scheme applies to acquisition proceedings for its stated purpose that began under the general acquisition law before the special scheme commenced, provided no award had been made before the special scheme applied.
material_facts: The special scheme expressly applied to earlier proceedings for its stated welfare purpose where no award had been made before the special scheme commenced.
The Court noted that the earlier judgment striking down the special scheme had not been stayed and that proceedings might have been revived and completed in the meantime.
The Court clarified that the special scheme would have no effect in cases where awards had already been made.
issues.conclusion: The special scheme applied to qualifying pending proceedings, but did not affect cases in which an award had already been made.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the transitional provision governing pending acquisition proceedings, read with the provision making the special scheme the exclusive means of acquisition for the specified purpose. It clarified that the transitional provision could not affect cases in which awards had already been made.

predicates.acquisition_proceeding_for_covered_welfa: The proceeding concerns acquisition of land for a welfare purpose covered by the special scheme.
predicates.proceeding_started_before_special_scheme: The acquisition proceeding began under the general acquisition process before the special scheme commenced.
predicates.no_award_made_before_special_scheme_appl: No award had been made in the proceeding before the special scheme applied to it.

issues.definition: If a proceeding for a covered welfare purpose began under the general process before the special scheme and no award had yet been made when the scheme applied, the special scheme governs that pending proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: Once a special acquisition scheme governs land required for its specified purpose, the State cannot acquire that land for the same purpose under the general acquisition law.
material_facts: Land was sought to be acquired under the general acquisition law for a purpose covered by the special acquisition scheme after that scheme had come into force.
The special scheme provided that land required for its specified purpose could be acquired only under its own provisions.
The special scheme was held valid apart from its requirement for payment of compensation in instalments.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings under the general acquisition law were quashed because the valid special scheme precluded acquisition for the covered purpose under that law.
issues.legal_principle: The exclusivity provision of the special acquisition scheme displaced the general acquisition law for land required for the specified purpose. Because the special scheme remained valid apart from its severed instalment-payment requirement, acquisition for that purpose had to proceed under the special scheme.

predicates.special_acquisition_scheme_is_in_force: A valid special statutory acquisition scheme governs the relevant kind of land acquisition.
predicates.land_is_required_for_purpose_covered_by_: The land is required for a purpose specified in the special scheme.
predicates.general_law_acquisition_is_started_for_t: The State starts or continues acquisition under the general process for that specified purpose.

issues.definition: If a valid special scheme governs land required for a covered purpose, a proceeding under the general acquisition process for that purpose is invalid.
